name: SQUID-amplified piezoresistive cantilever torque magnetometry (dHvA) of PdRhO2 at 700 mK up to 15 T in a dilution refrigerator
plain_name: Measure a tiny crystal's magnetic twist with a SQUID-read cantilever
description: Mount a 300 x 200 x 50 um PdRhO2 crystal on a PRC400 piezoresistive micro-cantilever on a rotator thermally anchored to the mixing chamber of an Oxford Instruments MX400 dilution refrigerator with a 15 + 2 T magnet; read the cantilever Wheatstone bridge with a two-stage dc-SQUID null detector and record de Haas-van Alphen torque at (700 +/- 20) mK during 30 mT/min down-sweeps from 15 T.
keywords: Measure a tiny crystal's magnetic twist with a SQUID-read cantilever

sources.citation: F. Arnold, M. Naumann, Th. Lühmann, A.P. Mackenzie, E. Hassinger, 'Application of SQUIDs to low temperature and high magnetic field measurements - Ultra low noise torque magnetometry', arXiv:1706.08350

requirements.rationale: The reported dHvA torque data were taken at (700 +/- 20) mK.
The field sweeps start at 15 T.
The torque sensor is a piezoresistive cantilever read as a resistance bridge, so electrical leads to the sample stage are required.
Optional: the documented down-sweep rate was 30 mT/min (= 0.5 mT/s).
Optional: lower-temperature operation to about 200 mK is possible with reduced excitation.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
